info.title: rooster API
info.description:
The REST API of a rooster instance: a keyboard-first, self-hosted task manager.

## Quick start

1. Create a personal access token in **Settings → Connected apps** (or `rooster token create my-script --scope tasks:read,tasks:write`). It is shown once.
2. Send it as a bearer token:

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROOSTER_TOKEN" https://rooster.example.com/api/v1/me

curl -X POST https://rooster.example.com/api/v1/orgs/personal/tasks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROOSTER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"title": "Pay invoice tomorrow >Prio", "parse": true}'
```

The `rooster` CLI wraps this API (`rooster login`, `rooster add "Pay invoice tom >Prio"`, `rooster ls --json`), and `@rooster/api-client` is a typed TypeScript client generated from this document.

## Authentication

- **Browser session cookie:** everything, including settings, org administration, admin, export, push subscriptions and creating tokens.
- **Bearer credentials** (a CLI device session or a PAT) carry a grant: capabilities such as `tasks:read` and `tasks:write`, limited to chosen orgs and groups. A missing capability is `403 forbidden_scope`, a target outside the grant `403 outside_grant`, an org or task the grant cannot see `404`. Browser-only routes answer `403 forbidden_scope`.
- **`/api/auth/*`** (better-auth: sign-in, OAuth callbacks, sign-out) is for the browser cookie only; bearer and PAT credentials get `403` there. The exceptions are `POST /api/auth/device/code` and `POST /api/auth/device/token` (form or JSON bodies), the unauthenticated RFC 8628 device flow endpoints that `rooster login` uses. These routes are not part of this document.

## Conventions

- **JSON only**, UTF-8. Timestamps are ms epoch numbers, dates `YYYY-MM-DD` (floating, no timezone), times `HH:MM`. IDs are UUIDv7; clients may supply `id` on create.
- **Errors** are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`; each operation lists its codes per status. `422 validation_failed` carries `errors: [{path, message}]`. Every response has an `X-Request-Id` header to quote in bug reports.
- **Writes** accept `Idempotency-Key` (safe retries), `X-Rooster-Edit-Time` (per-field last write wins), `X-Rooster-Client-Id` and `X-Rooster-Client`.
- **Ordering** is computed by the server: send `afterId` (the item directly above) and `beforeId` (the item directly below); never positions.
- **Pagination** is cursor based: `?limit=…&cursor=…` answers `{items, nextCursor}`; `nextCursor` is null on the last page.
- **Rate limits:** 600 requests per minute per user (`429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`).
- **Org IDs:** `{orgId}` accepts an org ID, its slug, or `personal`. Orgs you are not a member of are always `404`.
- **Versioning:** v1 changes are additive only; breaking changes would get `/api/v2`.

Grant.description: One PAT, CLI device or (Phase 9) OAuth client authorization: capabilities (`scopes`) plus `constraints`.

GrantConstraints.description: Where a grant may act (11 §2.2): `orgs: "all"` (including orgs joined later) or a list of orgs, each with `read` (`"all"` or `{groups}`) and `write` (`"none"`, `"all"` or `{groups}`). Groups are the user’s own groups; a task counts as being in the group where it sits in the user’s My tasks (a subtask: where its row sits).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a mutation safe to retry: a replay with the same key within 7 days returns the original status and body (with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) without running it again. The same key on a different request is `422 idempotency_key_reuse`. 1–128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; a UUID is a good choice.

EditTime.name: X-Rooster-Edit-Time
EditTime.description: When the user made the edit (ms epoch), for per-field last-write-wins: a field older than the stored edit is skipped and listed in `ignoredFields`. Defaults to the server’s clock; clamped to [now − 30 days, now + 5 s]. Offline clients send the original edit time when they replay.

ClientId.name: X-Rooster-Client-Id
ClientId.description: Identifies one client instance (a browser tab or a process); echoed as `origin` in the `invalidate` events this request causes, so the client can skip refetching its own change. 1–64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.

Client.name: X-Rooster-Client
Client.description: The kind of client and its version, recorded as `via` in activity entries: `web`, `pwa`, `cli`, `tui` or `mcp`, optionally followed by `/<version>`.

cookieSession.name: rooster.session
cookieSession.description: The browser session set by signing in at `/api/auth/*` (named `__Host-rooster.session` on https). **CSRF:** with cookie auth, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` must send an `Origin` header equal to the instance URL (`403 csrf_origin`) and a JSON body (`415 unsupported_media_type`). It is the only credential for settings, org administration, admin, export, push and token routes (others get `403 forbidden_scope`).

bearerSession.description: A session token from the CLI device flow (`rooster login`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Bearer requests are exempt from the CSRF Origin rule. The token carries a grant: capabilities and org/group constraints (`403 forbidden_scope`, `403 outside_grant`).

personalAccessToken.description: A personal access token created in Settings → Connected apps or with `rooster token create`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer rooster_pat_…`. Like a device session it carries a grant: a missing capability is `403 forbidden_scope`, a target outside its orgs or groups `403 outside_grant`.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds until the next request is allowed.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when this is the stored response of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events: hello, invalidations, notifications and heartbeats
get.description:
A `text/event-stream` (04 §4.5). Every message has `event:`, `data:` (JSON) and a
monotonic `id:` (per server process; there is no replay, so `Last-Event-ID` is ignored and
clients refetch their active queries after a reconnect).

- `hello` (first message): [`SseHello`](#/components/schemas/SseHello), the server version
  for update detection and its clock.
- `invalidate`: [`SseInvalidate`](#/components/schemas/SseInvalidate), query-key prefixes
  to invalidate verbatim. Only the affected users receive it. `origin` is the
  `X-Rooster-Client-Id` of the request that caused it, sent only to that user (null for
  everyone else). Bursts within ~50 ms are coalesced.
- `notification`: [`SseNotification`](#/components/schemas/SseNotification), only to the
  recipient: the unread count, with a preview of a new notification (null when only the
  count changed, e.g. after marking read on another device). Not coalesced.
- `: ping` comment every 25 s.

The stream ends on sign-out, session revoke, user deactivation and server shutdown. A
session keeps at most 4 streams and a user 12: opening one more
closes the oldest.
